title: read-only is silently overridden by an overlapping allowed dir

provenance.found_by: NorthWoods Sentinel Labs (NWS swarm, run by Margin, for Rob Chuvala)
provenance.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029 (NWS execution-boundary review, round 2, against cortex v6.13.0)

finding: const inReadOnly = !inAllowed && policy.readOnlyDirs.some(...), and the write-deny only fires on WRITE_TOOLS.has(toolName) && inReadOnly. inReadOnly can only be true when !inAllowed. When a path is inside both a broad allowedDirs entry and a nested readOnlyDirs entry, inAllowed wins, inReadOnly is false, and the write-deny never fires. The common policy "workspace writable, except this protected subdir" does not hold. Repro: allowedDirs:["/repo"], readOnlyDirs:["/repo/.claude"] -> Write /repo/.claude/settings.json is allowed.

repros.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029, finding F1

captured_on.note: Backfilled after the fact (assay environment-attestation fix, prompted by Rob Chuvala/NWS: "what substrate were those captured on? If we didn't record it, we have cases locked against an unpinned baseline." — his question named the gap; this corpus originally answered it by capturing environment identity (OS/arch/kernel/bun/cortex-commit) under the wrong name, `SubstrateStamp` — see the ubiquitous-language fix that renamed it to `EnvironmentStamp` (lib/environment.ts) and added a genuine `substrate` field, meaning the coding harness (lib/substrate.ts), using the ecosystem's `HarnessId` vocabulary). This corpus's runner captured no environment stamp before the original fix, so the only thing honestly knowable is the date this case entered the corpus — from the corpus's own commit (2173581, 2026-07-27T11:57:28+12:00), NOT from provenance.date above (that's when the underlying finding was discovered, a different event). OS/arch/kernel/bun-version/cortex-commit were never recorded at capture time and are not reconstructable — do not infer them from the machine running this backfill, or from the cortex commit named in this case's `fix` field (that documents the FIX, not the verification environment). `substrate` (coding harness) is also left `null`: this case was in fact authored during a Claude Code session — commit 2173581 carries a `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5` trailer, and the later environment-attestation commit 94e6598 carries a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_...` trailer, both consistent with Claude Code — but neither is a captured substrate stamp, so this is recollection backed by circumstantial commit evidence, not a record. Left `null` rather than asserted `claude-code`, per this corpus's own no-guessing rule. environment_digest and environment_provider_digest are `null` for a reason that postdates this case entirely: the field was added when the infrastructure factory's environment contract landed (environments/README.md), and no factory-built machine existed when this case was captured. There is nothing recorded and nothing reconstructable — a digest cannot be inferred after the fact from a machine that was never fingerprinted, which is the whole point of it being a digest. This case stays on the unpinned-baseline count until it is re-established on a factory VM.

expected: When a candidate path is contained in both an allowedDirs entry and a readOnlyDirs entry (exact match or nesting either direction), decidePath must resolve the overlap as read-only for every write tool (deny-precedence) — a narrower writable carve-out nested inside a broader read-only root must not regain write access.

fix.summary: decidePath now computes inAllowed and inReadOnly INDEPENDENTLY (no longer `!inAllowed && ...`), and read-only wins on any containment overlap (deny-precedence, not most-specific-match) — closes both the exact-match and the nested case.

verification.note: Unit-imports decidePath from path-guard.hook.ts and calls it directly with the finding's own repro shape (an allowedDirs root containing a nested readOnlyDirs entry), against a real temp-dir fixture standing in for /repo and /repo/.claude. Asserts Write is now denied.
